name: Heman
bio: Heman son of Joel was a Levite of the Kohathite clan. When David organized the Levites to carry the ark into Jerusalem with music and singing, Heman was named first among the three chief singers, alongside Asaph and Ethan, sounding bronze cymbals as the procession moved toward the city (1 Chronicles 15:16-19). While Asaph remained in Jerusalem to minister before the ark, Heman and Jeduthun served alongside Zadok and the priests at the old tabernacle in Gibeon, giving thanks to the LORD with trumpets, cymbals, and other instruments (1 Chronicles 16:39-42). He went on to lead Israel's worship for the rest of David's reign and is credited as the namesake of Psalm 88. David and his army commanders later set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun for musical service in the temple; Heman himself is described there as "the king's seer in the words of God," and God gave him fourteen sons and three daughters, all trained in song under their father (1 Chronicles 25:1-6).
